mainTopic: Worn coins: how much wear matters, what to do with an unusable coin, deadlines for returning one, and using it for מעשר שני
overview: The גמרא continues discussing a worn-down סלע. Two sources seem to show that a coin worn beyond the measure of אונאה may still be used, and the גמרא pushes both off. It then settles a contradiction between two ברייתות about piercing a worn coin and hanging it on a child's neck: it is allowed if the hole is in the middle, and forbidden if the hole is at the side. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's deadlines for returning a worn coin in cities and in villages. אביי and רבא explain differently why a garment is treated differently. The twelve-month rule is explained by רב חסדא as מידת חסידות, and the grievance clause is read as being about an ordinary person who refuses. רב פפא learns that someone too fussy about coins that still circulate is a נפש רעה. Finally the גמרא clarifies חזקיה: a worn coin may redeem מעשר שני, but only at its real value. It then begins a challenge to חזקיה's rule about produce worth less than a פרוטה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to prove that a coin worn beyond the measure of אונאה may still be sold
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'more than that, he sells it at its value,' the גמרא tries to show the ברייתא is talking about a coin that lost more than the measure of אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'More than that, he sells it at its value.' Doesn't this mean the coin lost more than its measure of אונאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of a ברייתא and tries to prove from it that a coin worn more than the measure of אונאה can still be sold for what it is really worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on one word, 'יתר' (more). The גמרא assumes 'more than that' means more wear than the measure of אונאה. If so, the ברייתא allows such a coin to be sold at its real value.

keyTerms.meaning: More than that / beyond that
He sells it at its actual value
Doesn't it mean...? (a formula for trying to prove something)
The measure of its אונאה (the amount of overcharging that counts as cheating)

phrases.english: More than that, he sells it at its value.
What, is it not that it eroded
more than its measure of exploitation?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו: שֶׁפָּחֲתָה יוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי אוֹנָאָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof from a ברייתא quoted before this section
steps.raayaObject: That a coin worn beyond the measure of אונאה may still be sold at its real value
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'יתר על כן מוכרה בשויה'

steps.title: Reading 'more than that' differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'More than that' is not about more wear. It is a stronger statement: even a coin that has not yet worn down to the measure of אונאה is sold only at its real value.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'More than that' means: even when it has not yet worn down to its measure of אונאה, he sells it at its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by giving the word 'יתר' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'יתר על כן' means 'going even further,' not 'worn down more.' So the ברייתא says nothing about a coin worn beyond the measure of אונאה, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Going further (in this reading, a stronger statement, not more wear)
Still / not yet

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'יתר' here as 'more wear.' The דחיה turns it into 'even more than that,' meaning the ruling applies even to a coin with less wear.

phrases.english: No, 'greater' means:
that it still did not erode to its measure of exploitation,
he sells it at its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by reading the word differently
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'יתר' means more wear. It can instead mean 'going even further.'

steps.title: Challenge: a סלע may be kept even after losing half its value
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a סלע may be kept until it wears down to a שקל, which is half its value. The גמרא assumes the coin wore down little by little, so it was kept even though it lost far more than the measure of אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: How much can it wear down and he may still keep it? For a סלע, up to a שקל. Doesn't this mean it wore down little by little?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to allow keeping a coin that lost much more than the measure of אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שקל is half a סלע, which is far more wear than the measure of אונאה. If the coin wore down slowly, the ברייתא would be allowing a badly worn coin to stay in use.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (bringing a source against an opinion)
To keep it (and use it)
A coin worth two שקלים
Little by little

phrases.english: They challenged: To what extent can it erode,
and he still be permitted to keep it?
For a sela, up to a shekel.
phrases.notes: A שקל is half a סלע, so the coin has lost half its value.

phrases.english: What, is it not that it eroded little by little!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, brings a second source
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that a coin worn beyond the measure of אונאה may not be kept in use
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows keeping a סלע worn down to half its value, which is far beyond the measure of אונאה.

steps.title: The coin lost its value all at once in a fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a coin that fell into a fire and lost its value in one go, not slowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about a coin that fell into the fire and wore down all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the challenge by explaining that the ברייתא is talking about a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the coin wore down slowly. The גמרא says the ברייתא is about a coin damaged all at once, in a fire. So the ברייתא does not show that a coin worn slowly beyond the measure of אונאה may be kept.

keyTerms.meaning: It fell into the fire
All at once, in one time

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is pushed off and the challenge is answered. 'יתר על כן' is read as 'going even further,' and the 'up to a שקל' ruling is about a coin that lost its value all at once in a fire, not one that wore down slowly.

phrases.english: No, it is where it fell into the fire
and eroded all at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 3 by narrowing its case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to a coin damaged suddenly
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge wrongly assumed the coin wore down little by little.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case: a coin damaged all at once in a fire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow keeping a סלע that wore down slowly to half its value, far beyond the measure of אונאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'up to a שקל' ruling is only about a coin that lost its value all at once in a fire. It says nothing about a coin that wore down slowly beyond the measure of אונאה.

steps.title: Quoting the ruling: make a hole in the coin and hang it on a child's neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא: a worn coin may be pierced and hung on a son's or daughter's neck. This sets up a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He should make a hole in it and hang it on the neck of his son or the neck of his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ruling about what to do with a worn coin. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coin is hung as jewelry, it is out of use as money. The גמרא quotes this ruling only so that it can set it against another ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting a line from an earlier source)
He should make a hole in it
And hang it

phrases.english: The Master said: He should perforate it
and suspend it on the neck of his son
or on the neck of his daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יִקֳּבֶנָּה וְיִתְלֶנָּה בְּצַוַּאר בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new detail of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn coin may be pierced and hung on a child's neck as jewelry.

steps.title: Another ברייתא forbids hanging the coin on a child's neck
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says not to use a worn coin as a weight, throw it in with scrap metal, or pierce it and hang it on a child's neck. Instead he must grind it, melt it, cut it up, or throw it into ים המלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: He should not make it a weight among his weights, nor throw it among his scraps, nor pierce it and hang it on the neck of his son and daughter. Rather, he should grind it, melt it, cut it, or take it to ים המלח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the ruling from step 5 against a ברייתא that clearly forbids the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא forbids every way of keeping the coin and allows only destroying it or getting rid of it completely. So it directly argues with the first ברייתא, which allowed hanging it on a child's neck.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction
His scraps of metal
He should grind it
He should melt it
The Dead Sea

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: He should not make it a weight
among his weights,
nor cast it among his metal scraps,
nor perforate it and suspend it
on the neck of his son and the neck of his daughter.
Rather: either he grinds it, or melts it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ יָקוֹץ, אוֹ יוֹלִיךְ לְיָם הַמֶּלַח!
phrases.english: or cuts it, or takes it to the Dead Sea!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂנָּה מִשְׁקָל בֵּין מִשְׁקְלוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ruling quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a worn coin may be pierced and hung on a child's neck
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא forbids exactly that and allows only destroying or discarding the coin.

steps.title: It depends where the hole is made: in the middle or at the side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (or רב הונא in רבי אלעזר's name) answers that hanging is allowed when the hole is in the middle of the coin and forbidden when the hole is at the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said, and some say רב הונא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: It is not difficult. Here, the hole is in the middle; there, the hole is at the side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the contradiction by explaining that the two ברייתות are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources do not really argue. The ruling that allows hanging is about a coin pierced in the middle. The ruling that forbids it is about a coin pierced near the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
In the middle
At the side, near the edge

steps.whatToRemember: A worn coin pierced in the middle may be hung as jewelry. A coin pierced at the side may not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna said that Rabbi Elazar said,
It is not difficult:
Here, in the middle,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ruling that allows hanging the coin; the hole was made in the middle.

phrases.english: there, from the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן – בָּאֶמְצַע, כָּאן – מִן הַצַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different kind of hole
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue about whether a worn coin may be hung as jewelry.
steps.terutzMaskana: Allowed when the hole is in the middle, forbidden when the hole is at the side.

steps.title: The time limit for returning a worn coin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in cities, a worn coin may be returned until there was time to show it to a money changer. In villages, the limit is until Friday (ערב שבת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when may one return a worn coin? In the cities, until there was time to show it to a money changer. In the villages, until the eve of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה about how long a person has to return a worn coin. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about how much a coin must be worn down. Now the topic is timing. The משנה gives two different time limits: one for cities and one for villages.

keyTerms.meaning: Big cities
Villages
Money changer, an expert in coins
Fridays, the days before שבת

phrases.english: Until when is it permitted to return [a worn coin]?
In the cities? Until enough time passes to show it to the money changer.
In the villages? Until the eves of שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how worn a coin must be to how long one has to return it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cities: until time to show a money changer. Villages: until ערב שבת.

steps.title: Why split cities and villages for a coin but not for a garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה makes a city/village difference for a סלע but gives one time limit for a garment (טלית) without any such difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a סלע, that the תנא makes a difference between cities and villages, and what is different about a garment, that he does not make that difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the rules for a coin and for a garment do not seem consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, the משנה gave one time limit for returning an overpriced garment, with no mention of cities or villages. Here, for a coin, it splits them. The גמרא wants to know why the two cases are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
He makes a distinction
A garment

phrases.english: What is different about a סלע, that he distinguishes [between cities and villages],
and what is different about a garment, that he does not distinguish?
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier משנה in this פרק about returning a garment that was sold for the wrong price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the city/village split just quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the coin rule (split by place) and the garment rule (not split).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If place matters for a coin, it should matter for a garment too, so why does only the coin rule mention it?

steps.title: אביי: the garment rule is only about cities
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the garment rule in the משנה was also said about cities. In villages the garment rule would be different too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even when we learned the משנה about a garment, we learned it about cities.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by saying the two rules really are the same. The garment rule was just talking about cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי removes the difference. The garment משנה simply did not mention villages, but it was speaking about cities. In a village, a garment would also get a longer time to be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Our משנה

phrases.english: אביי said:
Even when we learned our משנה
about a garment, it was about cities that we learned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the garment משנה to a specific case (cities).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garment rule applies everywhere, so it truly differs from the coin rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment rule is only about cities; there is no real difference between the two rules.

steps.title: רבא: everyone knows a garment's value, but only experts know a coin's
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: anyone can tell what a garment is worth, so place does not matter. A coin's value is known only to a money changer, so the time limit depends on whether one is around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A garment, every person knows its value. A סלע, since not every person knows its value, only a money changer, therefore in cities, where there is a money changer, until he can show it to the money changer. In villages, where there is no money changer, until the eves of שבת, when people go to the market.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer. He says the coin and the garment really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike אביי, רבא keeps the difference and explains it. Anyone can check a garment's value, so the buyer finds out quickly no matter where he lives. A coin needs an expert, so the time depends on when the buyer can reach one: right away in a city, or on Friday at the market in a village.

keyTerms.meaning: He knows its value well
Therefore
The market

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the garment rule was only about cities, so the two rules match. רבא: the rules really differ, because anyone can judge a garment, but only a money changer can judge a coin.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: טַלִּית, כֹּל אִינִישׁ קִים לֵיהּ בְּגַוַּהּ.
phrases.english: A garment, every person knows its value.

phrases.aramaic: סֶלַע, כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו כֹּל אִינִישׁ קִים לֵיהּ בְּגַוַּהּ
phrases.english: A סלע, since not every person knows its value
but only a money changer does,
therefore in the cities, where there is a money changer,
[he may return it] until there was time to show it to the money changer.
In the villages, where there is no money changer,
until the eves of שבת, when people go up to the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: טַלִּית, כֹּל אִינִישׁ קִים לֵיהּ בְּגַוַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 9, disagreeing with אביי's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a real reason for the difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A coin and a garment should get the same time limits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time limit depends on when the buyer can find out the true value: right away for a garment, but only through a money changer for a coin.

steps.title: A recognized coin may be returned even after a year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the one who gave the coin recognizes it, he must take it back even after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he recognized it, even after twelve months, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line seems to give a much longer time to return the coin than the limits just discussed. The גמרא is about to point out that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He recognizes it (as the coin he gave)
Twelve months

phrases.english: And if he recognized it

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: even after twelve months, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה line: he must take it back, and the other person has only a grievance against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה מַכִּירָהּ אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the giver recognizes the coin, he takes it back even after twelve months.

steps.title: Twelve months contradicts the short time limits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this case happened. In a city the limit is showing a money changer, and in a village it is ערב שבת, so how can the משנה allow twelve months?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where? If in the cities, didn't you say until there was time to show the money changer? If in the villages, didn't you say until the eves of שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the twelve-month line, because it seems to go against the time limits the משנה just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every place has already been given a short deadline. Either way, twelve months is far past it. So the two parts of the משנה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?
But you said

phrases.english: Where [did this happen]?
If in the cities, didn't you say
until there was time to show it to the money changer?
If in the villages, didn't you say
until the eves of שבת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 12 using the rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The twelve-month rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cities and villages already have short deadlines, so there is no place where twelve months could apply.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the twelve months is extra piety
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the twelve-month rule is not the strict law. It is מידת חסידות, going beyond what the law requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They taught a measure of piety here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction by saying the twelve-month line is about extra piety, not strict law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law, the short deadlines still apply. But a pious person who recognizes his coin takes it back even a year later. So the two parts of the משנה no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of piety, doing more than the law requires
They taught here

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
They taught a measure of piety here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִידַּת חֲסִידוּת שָׁנוּ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the rule as beyond-the-law piety rather than strict law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The twelve-month rule is the basic law, so it contradicts the deadlines.
steps.terutzMaskana: The deadlines are the law; the twelve-month rule is only מידת חסידות.

steps.title: If it is only piety, who has the grievance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the end of the משנה, which says there is only a grievance (תרעומת). Neither person seems to have a reason for a grievance if this is just piety.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say the end of the משנה: He has against him only a grievance. For whom? If for the pious one, let him not accept the coin and not have a grievance. Rather, for the one from whom he accepted it? After the coin was accepted from him, should he have a grievance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer using the last words of the משנה about a grievance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If taking the coin back is optional piety, a pious person who is upset can just say no, so he has no grievance. And the other person got his coin taken back, so he has nothing to complain about either. The משנה's mention of a grievance does not seem to fit רב חסדא's reading; the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end of the משנה
A grievance, a complaint without legal force
A pious person
For whom?

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two people straight: the חסיד is the one who first gave the coin and now takes it back. The other person is the one who received it and is returning it.

phrases.english: If so, say the end [of the משנה]:
He has against him only a grievance.
For whom?
If for the pious one,
let him just not accept it from him,
and let him not have a grievance.
Rather, for that one from whom he accepted it?
But after he accepted it from him,
should he have a grievance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: אֵין לוֹ עָלָיו אֶלָּא תַּרְעוֹמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the twelve-month rule is מידת חסידות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה speaks of a grievance, but under a piety reading neither the pious giver nor the person returning the coin has any reason to complain.

steps.title: The grievance applies to an ordinary person, not a pious one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the end of the משנה. The twelve-month rule is for a pious person. An ordinary person who refuses to take the coin back cannot be forced, and the other side only has a grievance against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: but another person, even though he does not take the coin back from him, the other side has only a grievance against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 15 by showing that the 'grievance' line is talking about a different person than the חסיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if taking the coin back is only piety, why would anyone have a grievance? The answer is that the משנה is describing two people. The pious one takes the coin back even after twelve months. Another, ordinary person may refuse, and then the one stuck with the coin can only complain. He cannot force him in court.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא is explaining how to read the text)
Another person, here meaning an ordinary person, not a חסיד
A grievance or complaint, with no legal power to force anything

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two levels. Strict law: no obligation after the time limit. מידת חסידות: take the coin back even after twelve months. If someone refuses, the other side has only a תרעומת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב חסדא's explanation that the twelve-month rule is only מידת חסידות.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
But another person,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ –
phrases.english: even though he does not accept it back from him,
he has only a grievance against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15 against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: the grievance clause is about a different person (an ordinary person, not the חסיד).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grievance clause seemed to be about the same pious case, so a grievance made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pious person takes the coin back after twelve months. An ordinary person who refuses leaves the other side with only a grievance.

steps.title: The eroded coin may be used to redeem מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the slightly eroded coin may be used to redeem מעשר שני without worry, because anyone who refuses it is only a miserly person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may give the coin for מעשר שני, and he need not worry, because the one who refuses it is only a miserly soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. This sets up רב פפא's lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coin has lost only a little weight, so it is still a valid coin. It may be used to redeem מעשר שני produce. If someone rejects it, the problem is his own stinginess, not the coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that can be redeemed onto money
He need not worry
A miserly, stingy person (literally 'a bad soul')

phrases.english: And he may give it for second tithe,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the slightly eroded coin. He uses it to redeem מעשר שני produce.

phrases.english: and he need not worry,
for it is only a miserly soul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slightly eroded coin may be used for redeeming מעשר שני. Refusing it is just stinginess.

steps.title: רב פפא: being too fussy about coins is called miserly
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the משנה's wording that a person who is overly strict about his coins is called a נפש רעה. The גמרא adds that this applies only when the coins he rejects are still being used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: learn from this that someone who is overly strict about his coins is called a miserly soul. And this applies only when those coins are still in use.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a practical lesson from the משנה's wording, and the גמרא adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה calls the person who refuses the coin a נפש רעה, רב פפא learns that being overly picky about coins is a character flaw. The limit: this is only true if people still use those coins. If they do not, refusing them is reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a lesson drawn from the text)
Is strict about his coins
And this applies only (introduces a limit)
Circulate, are in use

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying a person must accept any damaged coin. The criticism applies only when the coins are still being used by people.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this:
one who is strict about his coins,
phrases.notes: He means someone who will only take perfect, undamaged coins.

phrases.english: is called a miserly soul.
And this applies only when they circulate.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the flawed coins he refuses. If people still spend them, refusing them is just stinginess.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the wording 'נפש רעה' in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who insists on perfect coins is called a נפש רעה, but only when the coins he rejects still circulate.

steps.title: The משנה supports חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה supports חזקיה. He taught that when exchanging the eroded coin, it is counted at its true value, but when redeeming מעשר שני with it, it is treated as a good coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports חזקיה, who said: if he comes to exchange the coin, he exchanges it for what it is worth. If he comes to redeem with it, he redeems as if it were a full, good coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of חזקיה and says the משנה backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the eroded coin to be used for מעשר שני. חזקיה said the same: for redeeming, the coin counts as a full coin. When simply exchanging it for smaller coins, though, you count only its real, reduced value.

keyTerms.meaning: Supports him
To exchange it for smaller change
At its actual worth
To redeem with it (מעשר שני)
As a good, full coin

phrases.english: This supports Chizkiyah,
as Chizkiyah said:
If he comes to exchange it, he exchanges it at its value;
if he comes to redeem with it, he redeems as with a good coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the משנה's rule about מעשר שני to חזקיה's statement.
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's ruling that an eroded coin redeems מעשר שני as a full coin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'ונותנה למעשר שני ואינו חושש'.

steps.title: What is חזקיה adding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חזקיה is really saying. It seems he is just repeating the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of חזקיה's statement. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חזקיה only said what the משנה already says, his statement adds nothing. The גמרא wants to know what new point he is making.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (asking for the meaning)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of חזקיה's statement just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point חזקיה's statement makes beyond the משנה.

steps.title: Even though it is exchanged at its true value, it redeems as a full coin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains חזקיה: even though, when he later exchanges the coin, he gets only its true reduced value, he still may redeem מעשר שני with it as if it were a full coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: even though when he comes to exchange it, he gets only what it is worth, when he redeems with it, he redeems as with a good coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing that חזקיה's two halves are one connected statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it looked like two separate rules. Now we read them together. The coin's lower exchange value does not stop it from redeeming מעשר שני as a full coin. That is the new point חזקיה adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though

steps.whatToRemember: For now, חזקיה's statement is read as one connected rule: the coin is exchanged at its reduced value, yet it may be used to redeem מעשר שני. Steps 22–23 clarify that even then it counts only at its real value.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כְּשֶׁבָּא לְפוֹרְטָהּ – פּוֹרְטָהּ בְּשׇׁוְיָהּ,
phrases.english: Even though when he comes to exchange it, he exchanges it at its value,
when he redeems with it, he redeems as with a good coin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי כְּשֶׁבָּא לְפוֹרְטָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיה's two clauses are connected: even though the coin is exchanged at its reduced value, it still redeems מעשר שני as a full coin.

steps.title: Does חזקיה really allow shortchanging מעשר שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's ruling from his own teaching elsewhere, which shows he is careful never to shortchange מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean חזקיה holds that we may treat מעשר שני lightly? But חזקיה himself said: if מעשר שני produce is worth less than a פרוטה, one says, 'It and its fifth are redeemed on the first coins,' because a person can never be perfectly exact with his coins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two teachings of חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, חזקיה let a worn coin redeem מעשר שני as if it were a full coin, which looks like giving מעשר שני less than it deserves. But in another teaching he says that tiny bits of produce may be redeemed on earlier coins, because those coins almost surely had a little extra value. That shows he cares that מעשר שני always gets its full value, so how can he allow a worn coin to count as full?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a surprising conclusion)
we treat lightly, we shortchange
worth a פרוטה, the smallest value that counts
its fifth, the extra amount an owner adds when redeeming his own produce
redeemed, its holiness moved onto the coins
to be exact, to measure precisely

phrases.english: Is that to say that חזקיה holds
that we may treat מעשר שני lightly?
phrases.notes: He means redeeming it for less than its true worth, like using a worn coin as if it were full.

phrases.english: But didn't חזקיה say:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה,
phrases.english: Second-tithe produce that is not worth a פרוטה,
one says: It and its fifth
are redeemed on the first coins.
phrases.notes: The 'first coins' are the ones he already used earlier to redeem other מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Because it is impossible for a person
to be exact with his coins!
phrases.notes: So the earlier coins probably had a little extra value, enough to cover this small amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of חזקיה given in step 21 using another teaching of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's ruling that a worn coin may redeem מעשר שני as a good coin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזקיה elsewhere insists that מעשר שני must get full value, even relying on leftover value in earlier coins; so he should not allow a worn coin to count as full.

steps.title: A valid coin, but counted at its real value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'ביפה' means the worn coin is accepted as a proper coin, but it is not also counted at full value, since we do not allow two leniencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'as a good coin' mean? It means it has the status of a good coin. But it is valued at what it is really worth, because we do not treat מעשר שני lightly in two ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining what חזקיה meant by 'as a good coin.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a worn coin at all is one leniency, and חזקיה allows that by treating it as a valid coin. Counting it at its old full value would be a second leniency, and that is not allowed. So מעשר שני still gets its true value, and there is no contradiction with חזקיה's other teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: what (does it mean)?
with the status of a good coin
two kinds of lowering or disrespect

steps.confusionAlert: Step 21 sounded like the worn coin counts as a full coin. Now the גמרא clarifies: it counts as a valid coin, but only at its real, reduced value.
steps.whatToRemember: A worn coin may redeem מעשר שני, but only for what it is truly worth. One leniency is allowed; two are not.

phrases.english: What does "as a good coin" mean?
With the status of a good coin.
Because two kinds of lowering
we do not do to it.
phrases.notes: Using a worn coin is one; counting it at full value would be a second, so that is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by reinterpreting the word 'ביפה'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'as a good coin' meant the worn coin counts at full value, which would shortchange מעשר שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only that the worn coin is a valid coin; it is still counted at its real value, so מעשר שני is not shortchanged.

steps.title: חזקיה's rule about produce worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at חזקיה's teaching about small amounts of מעשר שני on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: חזקיה said, if מעשר שני is worth less than a פרוטה, one says, 'It and its fifth are redeemed on the first coins,' because a person can never be perfectly exact with his coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to study חזקיה's teaching from step 22 by itself, setting it up so it can be challenged next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce worth less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed on new coins, because less than a פרוטה does not count. חזקיה's solution is to attach it to coins already used, since they likely hold a little extra value. The גמרא repeats this teaching now as the subject of a new discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself; now we study a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself.
חזקיה said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה,
phrases.english: Second-tithe produce that is not worth a פרוטה,
one says: "It and its fifth
are redeemed on the first coins,"
because it is impossible for a person
to be exact with his coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the teaching quoted in step 22 and opens a new discussion about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה, together with its fifth, may be redeemed on coins already used for earlier redemption, since those coins likely carry extra value.

steps.title: A challenge begins from תרומה and ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to bring a משנה to challenge חזקיה, beginning with the laws of תרומה and ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: For תרומה and ביכורים, a non-כהן is liable to death and to adding a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to חזקיה; this is only the opening of the משנה it quotes, and the point of the challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us a source is coming that seems to argue with חזקיה. So far it only lists that תרומה and ביכורים carry a death penalty and a fifth for one who eats them. The part that clashes with חזקיה's rule has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
the portion of produce given to a כהן
first fruits brought to the בית המקדש
death at the hands of Heaven
the added fifth paid for eating it by mistake

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Teruma and first fruits —
one is liable for them to death and a fifth,
phrases.notes: This is said about a non-כהן who eats them; the rest of the source continues in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against the teaching of חזקיה restated in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's rule that מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה can be redeemed on earlier coins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about תרומה and ביכורים is being introduced to contradict חזקיה; its decisive line comes after this point.
